title: Graff wins at Spa by 0.581s after late drive-through
dek: Richard Bradley, Gustavo Yacaman and James Allen won for Graff by 0.581 seconds from fifth on the grid, surviving a late drive-through penalty that had erased a lead of almost 20 seconds.

chapters.title: A title fight with two rounds to go
text: The 4 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps on 24 September was the penultimate round of the first European Le Mans Series season for the new generation of LMP2 cars, and the championship was tightening. G-Drive Racing by DragonSpeed arrived with a 12-point lead over United Autosports, whose Ligier JS P217 had won at Silverstone and the Red Bull Ring, while the Oreca had won at Monza. The Dallara P217 of SMP Racing had then taken its first victory at Le Castellet a month earlier, so three different crews had won the first four races.

The entry stood at 35 cars, twelve of them in LMP2, and several line-ups had changed. Ryo Hirakawa returned to the G-Drive Oreca #22 after his Super GT commitments in Japan had kept him away for two rounds, in which DragonSpeed sporting director Nicolas Minassian had deputised and helped bring two podiums. Paul-Loup Chatin took over the IDEC Sport Ligier #28 from Olivier Pla, who was racing in IMSA, and Jonathan Hirschi, a Manor driver in the World Endurance Championship, made his first ELMS start for Graff in the #39 Oreca in place of Eric Trouillet.

Practice offered no clear favourite. Hirschi topped a red-flagged first session in 2:04.796, 0.036 seconds ahead of Ben Hanley's DragonSpeed Oreca, before Hirakawa went quickest in the second on 2:03.058, with Graff's Yacaman second and Filipe Albuquerque's United Ligier third. The week also brought news from outside the paddock, as the rule-makers confirmed which of the LMP2 chassis would be allowed performance updates for 2018, with the Oreca receiving none.

chapters.title: Hanley puts DragonSpeed on pole
text: Ben Hanley took pole position for the DragonSpeed Oreca #21 with a lap of 2:02.457, the third pole of the season for the car he shares with Henrik Hedman and Nicolas Lapierre and the fourth for DragonSpeed overall. He said the first lap of the run was the one that mattered because tyre degradation at Spa is so high. Hirakawa made it an all-DragonSpeed front row, 0.375 seconds back in the G-Drive car on 2:02.832.

Enzo Guibbert completed an Oreca sweep of the top three for Graff on 2:03.053, and Albuquerque was fourth on 2:03.330 as the quickest of the Ligiers. Richard Bradley placed the second Graff Oreca, the #40, fifth on 2:03.427. Andrea Pizzitola was sixth for Algarve Pro Racing and Nathanaël Berthon seventh for Panis Barthez, with Chatin eighth in the IDEC Ligier.

It was a hard session for the Dallaras. SMP Racing's #27 was the best of them in ninth on 2:04.324, about 1.9 seconds off the pole time, ahead of Cetilar Villorba Corse and the Racing Team Nederland car. Elsewhere on the grid, AT Racing took LMP3 pole with Mikkel Jensen and Proton Competition's Matteo Cairoli took pole in LMGTE.

chapters.title: Pole-sitter drops to eleventh
text: Hanley's pole advantage did not last: the #21 car slipped as low as eleventh during the opening stint, while the Graff, United, SMP and Panis Barthez cars ran at the front of the class. The race was soon neutralised after a heavy accident for Andrea Roda at Pouhon, where the Algarve Pro Ligier #25 hit the barrier and rolled onto its roof. Roda walked away unharmed. Teams pitted at around the end of the first hour under the Safety Car, which shuffled the order and set the pattern for the day.

chapters.title: Splash-and-dash strategies
text: A succession of Full Course Yellows and Safety Car periods, most of them caused by incidents in LMP3 and LMGTE, ran through the middle of the race and split the field on strategy. DragonSpeed brought its cars in for a splash of fuel at the first opportunity, which left both Oreca #21 and the G-Drive car further back for long periods, while the Graff #40 led for Bradley, with the United Ligier, the SMP Dallara and, for a time, the Panis Barthez Ligier near the front. Panis Barthez then lost its place with a problem at a stop.

SMP's Egor Orudzhev drove the Dallara #27 for more than three hours before handing over to Matevos Isaakyan for the closing stint, an iron-man effort that he said had not been planned. On the DragonSpeed side Hedman and Hanley shared the pole-sitting car until the last ninety minutes, when Lapierre took over to try to fight back through the field.

chapters.title: Bradley holds on by 0.581 seconds
text: The decision came in the last hour as the leaders cycled through their final stops. Bradley, after a move around the outside at Les Combes on the SMP Dallara that took him off the track, had to serve a drive-through penalty for the overtake and lost a lead of almost 20 seconds. Hirakawa, who had to stretch a stint to 19 laps to save fuel, then chased the leader but got stuck in traffic.

Bradley took the flag 0.581 seconds clear to give the Graff #40 of Bradley, Yacaman and Allen its first LMP2 win. Hirakawa was second in the car that leads the standings, and SMP's Dallara was third, 16.069 seconds behind. The SMP result pushed the United Ligier #32 down to fourth, 17.018 seconds off the winner, and the pole-sitting #21 recovered from its early setback to finish fifth, 39.161 seconds back. The sister Graff, the #39, was sixth, with the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47 seventh.

chapters.title: Graff's breakthrough and a wider title lead
text: Graff's first victory in LMP2 came in its first season with the class, a year in which the team's two Orecas had shown speed but suffered a number of new-car problems. Bradley said the team had had the pace to win everywhere except Le Castellet. Orudzhev, whose long stint had put the SMP Dallara on the podium again, said he had expected to do around two and a half hours rather than more than three. Hirakawa said he had known he needed to push but had to save fuel while stuck behind slower cars.

The championship moved in G-Drive's favour. With United's car pushed back to fourth, the lead of Memo Rojas and Léo Roussel over Hugo de Sadeleer, Will Owen and Albuquerque grew from 12 to 18 points going into the finale at Portimão on 22 October. It was the fourth different winning line-up in five rounds of the new LMP2 era in the series.

Graff confirmed it would return to the series in 2018 with two Oreca 07s and intended to enter both at the Le Mans 24 Hours, having considered the WEC and dropped the plan. For the finale the #39 car would change drivers again, with Ricardo Sanchez replacing Hirschi, and Chatin was set to stay in the IDEC Ligier. The 2018 calendar was also announced, with Le Castellet moving to open the season on 14–15 April and Spa to host its round on 22–23 September.

Algarve Pro had a different race against time after Roda's crash had broken almost every body panel on the #25 car. The team made an 18-hour drive to Motorland Aragon, rebuilt the car and had it back in testing 72 hours later for its Asian Le Mans Series customers. Elsewhere the paddock looked ahead, as Yvan Muller said he was considering an LMP2 entry for his team and several of the 2017 LMP2 teams were planning to expand to two cars.

facts.v: The Graff Oreca #40 beat the G-Drive Oreca #22 by 0.581 seconds after losing a lead of almost 20 seconds to a drive-through penalty.
